title: Research best-effort F_7 packed encoding
description:
Prototype 2–4 candidate $\mathbb{F}_7$ packed encodings, measure cycles/op for each, and produce a decision document selecting the winning candidate that the implementation phase will instantiate.

## Background

⚠ **User approval required** before selecting the winning encoding — this is the input contract for the $\mathbb{F}_7$ implementation work.

$\mathbb{F}_7$ has 7 elements; the simplest baseline is 3-bit-per-element packed with one redundant codeword (16 elements per `u64`) and a $2^{16}$ LUT for mul. $\mathbb{F}_7^*$ is cyclic of order 6, which suggests a $(\log \bmod 6, \mathit{zero})$ representation may permit cheaper multiplication than mul-via-LUT. A 4-bit packed representation (8 elements per `u64`) may also let multiplication exploit XOR-structure on a non-redundant codeword.

This issue prototypes 2–4 candidate encodings in `dev/research/f7_packing/`, measures cycles/op, and produces a decision document.

Hard fallback if no novel encoding beats the LUT baseline by $\ge 1.5\times$: select the 3-bit + LUT baseline.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `dev/research/f7_packing/` exists and builds with `cargo build -p f7-packing-prototype --release`.
- [ ] [hard] At least 2 candidate encodings are implemented and benchmarked.
- [ ] [hard] `dev/plans/r2_f7_encoding_decision.md` exists and is attached via `jit doc add`, naming the winning candidate.
- [ ] [hard] The decision doc documents bitwise op counts for `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div` on the chosen encoding.
- [ ] [hard] The user has signed off (recorded as a comment) before transitioning to `done`.
